newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine CEI says could buy all Penaflor shares.
newsitem.headline: Argentine CEI says could buy all Penaflor shares.

text.p: Argentina's Citicorp Equity Investments (CEI) Tuesday said it is considering buying from local group Pulenta between half and all the shares of Penaflor winery, whose worth it estimated at $200 million.
CEI told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange it could buy between 51 percent and 100 percent of the Penaflor shares.
"The purchase option granted to Citicorp Equity Investments SA (CEI) by the shareholders of Penaflor SA envisages in principle a corporate worth of $200 million," it said in a statement.
Last week CEI said it had an option until December 31 to buy about 85 percent of the outstanding shares of Penaflor.

Press reports had said CEI was in talks with Pulenta to also purchase the mineral water unit Villa del Sur, brewery Cerveceria Bieckert and fruit juice firm Cepita. French group Danone has a 50 percent stake in Villa del Sur.
Meanwhile, Argentina's Quilmes Industrial SA said Monday it exercised an option to buy from Pulenta 85 percent of Bieckert.

The option to buy Bieckert, which had a 6.5 percent share of Argentina's brewing market in 1995, values Cerveceria at $40 million, including financial debt, Quilmes said. The purchase is still subject to certain conditions and to the completion of the due diligence process, it added.

CEI has said it had accepted an offer to buy for $590 million 920 million common shares of Compania de Inversiones en Telecomunicaciones SA (COINTEL), that has a controlling stake in Telefonica de Argentina.
